Where it began

Rachin Ravindra arrived on 18 November 1999 in Wellington. His parents came from Bangalore and had moved to New Zealand two years before. He started playing at five, grew up idolising Sachin Tendulkar, and went to Hutt International Boys' School. Most years he went back to India to play club cricket with the Hutt Hawks, a side his father ran.

He played at two Under-19 World Cups, in 2016 and 2018, and the second marked him out as one to watch. Wellington gave him a contract that year, and his first first-class hundred came in the Plunket Shield in March 2020.

The player

He made his Test debut against India in November 2021. His breakthrough with the bat came in February 2024, when he made 240 against South Africa batting at four. It was his first Test hundred, and no New Zealander had ever made a bigger one for his first. By October 2026 he had played 24 Tests and made 1,865 runs at 47.82, with five hundreds and seven fifties. With his left-arm spin he had taken 11 wickets, with a best of 3 for 33.

The one-day game made him famous. Brought into the 2023 World Cup squad late and pushed up to number three for the opening match, he made a hundred on his World Cup debut. He finished with three hundreds and 578 runs, the most anyone had made at his first World Cup, and won the ICC's Emerging Cricketer of the Year award.

What made him special

He showed a real taste for the big stage. In the 2025 Champions Trophy he made a hundred on debut there too, added another in the semi-final, and was named Player of the Tournament. At the 2026 T20 World Cup, when his batting was quieter, he turned to his spin and finished as New Zealand's leading wicket-taker.

By October 2026 his bowling in Tests had been a supporting act rather than the main event, at 47.91 a wicket. Nobody minded much, since he usually made up for it with the bat.

Away from the middle

On his first appearance for Durham in 2022 he turned a hundred into a double hundred, 217. He went on to play franchise cricket in the IPL and in Major League Cricket in the United States, and in October 2023 he was the ICC's Player of the Month.

And finally

As a boy he looked up to Tendulkar. At the 2023 World Cup he broke a couple of his hero's records for a young batter at the tournament, which seems a fine way to pay a compliment.
